evidence_summary: Effects Database's Guild catalog identifies the Stinger Gain Pedal as an Applied-built Guild product; it is retained as a distinct gain/booster family rather than folded into the FW-3 fuzz platform.

Effects Database lists a Guild Fuzz Box in the Applied branch. The builder relationship is retained, but the surviving catalog-level evidence is not yet sufficient to establish a precise production window or exact relationship to the earlier Goya/Applied fuzz families.

The Applied OEM wah index identifies Banshee Wah as an Applied product family member. The chronology remains separate from the FW-3 combination pedal because the wah is a dedicated single-effect platform.

Effects Database places the Guild VW-1 in the Applied Wah OEM family and specifically dates its Guild catalog appearance to 1972-1978. Retain it separately from the FW-3 even though both came from Applied.
The Applied Wah OEM index associates Hohner WW-20 with the Applied wah family, but current evidence does not establish a model-specific production statement comparable to Guild FW-3 or Guild VW-1.

model_or_family: SP-5 Siren and Surf & Turf Pedal
evidence_summary: Tone Machines documents the 1974 Guild SP-5 as an Applied-built U.S. reintroduction of the earlier Shin-Ei Surf Wah design, available in the June 1974 Guild catalog for a single year. This is a later U.S. reintroduction, not continuous Shin-Ei manufacture.

model_or_family: EX-1 Siren and Volume / Wah-Wah / Surf & Tornado
evidence_summary: Effects Database links V-Jay Model EX-1 to the Applied-built Guild SP-5 family and the later Hohner ME-30. Retained as a marketed state pending stronger period-specific documentation.

The Applied Wah OEM index groups Applied Banshee Wah, Crown Wah Wah, Guild VW-1, Jax-USA Wah, Kadent Wah Wah, Magnum Wah Wah, V-Jay Wah Wah and Hohner WW-20. This row is a family index only and is not a claim that all variants were identical or contemporaneous.
